title: The Gospel of Matthew
subtitle: Kata Maththaion, “According to Matthew”
description: The first book of the New Testament, which opens with a family line from Abraham through David to “Jesus, who is called Christ”, and shows again and again that in him the promises of Israel’s Scriptures were fulfilled. The wise men and their star; the Sermon on the Mount, with the beatitudes and the Lord’s Prayer; parables of the kingdom of heaven, from the mustard seed to the pearl of great price; Peter’s confession and the promise of the church; the sheep and the goats; the cross, the guarded tomb, and the risen Lord sending his disciples to make disciples of all the nations, with the promise “I myself am with you every day, until the close of the age.” In the Open Word Bible, a new translation from the Greek given freely to the public domain, with an introduction to the book’s shape and meaning and a conclusion on where to read next.

qa.question: What is the Gospel of Matthew?
qa.answer: The first of the four Gospels, the accounts of the life, death and resurrection of Jesus in the New Testament, and for most of the church’s history the most read of them. It presents Jesus as the son of David and the son of Abraham, Israel’s Messiah, in whom the Scriptures are fulfilled, and gathers his teaching into five long speeches, beginning with the Sermon on the Mount (chapters 5–7). It ends with the risen Jesus sending his disciples to all the nations (28:18–20).

qa.question: Who wrote the Gospel of Matthew, and when?
qa.answer: The Gospel does not name its author. From the second century the church gave it to Matthew, the tax collector who became one of the Twelve (9:9). Papias, early in the second century, said that Matthew wrote the oracles in the Hebrew language. Most scholars today think the author drew on Mark’s Gospel and date the book to the decades after AD 70; others hold that Matthew wrote first, or date it in the 60s.

qa.question: Why does Matthew say “kingdom of heaven” instead of “kingdom of God”?
qa.answer: Devout Jews often said “heaven” rather than speak the name of God too freely, and Matthew, writing as a Jew for readers who knew the Scriptures, follows their custom. The kingdom of heaven is not a different kingdom from the kingdom of God in Mark and Luke, and it does not mean only a place people go when they die. It is God’s own rule, which Jesus says “has come near” (4:17).

qa.question: What are the five speeches in Matthew?
qa.answer: Matthew gathers Jesus’s teaching into five long speeches, each ending with almost the same words, “When Jesus had finished”: the Sermon on the Mount (5–7), the sending of the Twelve (10), the parables of the kingdom (13), life together in the community of disciples (18), and the end of the age (24–25). Between them come stories of what Jesus did. Many readers have heard an echo of the five books of Moses.

qa.question: What does Matthew 16:18 mean by “on this rock I will build my church”?
qa.answer: Jesus plays on Peter’s name, which means rock, after Peter confesses him as the Christ, the Son of the living God. Christians have long differed on what the rock is: Peter himself, as the first of the apostles; the faith he has just confessed; or Christ, the only foundation. Matthew is the only Gospel in which Jesus speaks of the church, here and in 18:17.

qa.question: Which translation of the Bible is this?
qa.answer: The Open Word Bible, a new translation made directly from the Greek and dedicated to the public domain, printed here at its Balanced level, which aims to be accurate and to read naturally aloud. The reasoning behind each of its sentences, with the Greek beside it, is published at openwordbible.org. The introduction and conclusion were written for this edition.
